start.text: A ring of beach stones and a fire of driftwood in it, leaned up in a cone over a red heart the way a collier builds anything that has to last. A black kettle on a stone. A log for a seat, sat smooth.

The fog sits round it close and doesn't mind it, the way it sits round a clamp in the colliers' clearing. Sea's leavings. Whatever lets a collier's fire be lets this one be too. It doesn't push the fog back an inch.
The fire's been raked out and the stones kicked in over the ash, collier-fashion, so it won't creep. The kettle's still on its stone. Nobody's coming back for a kettle.
